The issue is about background style. When text is wrapped (or soft-wrapped), the background style should probably extend to the end of the line.

Wait, `soft_wrap=True` means it *doesn't* wrap. It just lets the line be as long as it wants.
The issue says "fix background style with soft wrap".
If `soft_wrap=True`, the text is not wrapped by `rich`, but it might be wrapped by the terminal.
If the terminal wraps it, the background style only applies to the text itself, not to the rest of the line.

However, if `rich` does the wrapping (e.g. `soft_wrap=False`), it can insert the background style on each line.

Let's see what happens when `soft_wrap=False` (default) and the text is long.

If the text has a background style, it's printed as `\x1b[41mText\x1b[0m`.
If the terminal wraps this, the second line will not have the background style.

But if `soft_wrap=False`, `rich` wraps it and prints:
`\x1b[41mLine 1\x1b[0m\n\x1b[41mLine 2\x1b[0m\n`

If the user wants `soft_wrap=True` but still wants the background style to be preserved across terminal wraps, that's not possible unless the terminal supports some specific feature.

This looks like it's for SVG export.

Let's go back to the issue. "background styles are not correctly maintained when `soft_wrap=True` is used".

If `soft_wrap=True`, `rich` does not wrap the text.
If the text has a background style, it's applied to the characters.
If the terminal wraps the text, the background style is only on the characters, not the whole line.

Wait, if `soft_wrap=False`, `rich` wraps the text.
When `rich` wraps the text, it creates multiple `Text` objects (one for each line).
If the original `Text` had a background style, each of these `Text` objects will have that background style.
And when `rich` prints a `Text` object, it prints the style, then the text, then resets the style.

If the `Text` object is exactly the width of the terminal, then the background style covers the whole line.
If the `Text` object is shorter than the terminal width, the background style only covers the text.

Wait, if `soft_wrap=False`, `rich` wraps the text to the `width` of the console.
So each line is exactly `width` characters long (except the last one).
Thus, the background style covers the whole line.

If `soft_wrap=True`, `rich` does NOT wrap the text. It prints one long line.
The terminal then wraps this long line.
The background style is only on the characters of that long line.
When the terminal wraps it, the background style is only on the characters, not the remaining space of the line.

But wait, if the background style is on the characters, and the characters fill the line, then the background style fills the line.
The problem is that the background style is only applied to the characters.
If the terminal wraps the text, the background style is only on the characters that were wrapped.
